originality.rationale: The result concerns scale-free inverse reconstruction of the radius and dihedral angle of surface-area-uniform spherical lunes from second and fourth ambient-chord moments. The closest inspected 2020 article gives forward intrinsic spherical distance distributions by geodesic chord distributions and explicitly works out spherical caps; it does not state or imply by any exhibited specialisation the global monotonic ratio for arbitrary-angle lunes. Tu–Fischbach studies ball-volume rather than spherical-surface sampling, Gille studies line-sampled chords, and Besau et al. study random hull facet counts. A previously obtained cap inverse theorem matches the hemisphere endpoint, but none of the open-angle lune classification or certified monotonicity follows from the cap family. Exact priority remains provisional, with residual unindexed-literature risk.

value.rationale: Two scale-covariant chord moments completely identify the unknown radius and angle of a natural geodesically convex spherical digon. Their dimensionless ratio decreases strictly even though the full chord distance increases in stochastic order; the exact attainable boundary and optimal inverse square-root exponent quantify a nontrivial geometric inverse instability. The new inequality and classification concern an entire continuum of lune angles rather than a routine special-function evaluation or a known hemisphere endpoint.
